sources.cite: AWS Lambda Developer Guide, Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: by default, after an error 'all messages in that batch return to the queue. After the visibility timeout, the messages become visible to Lambda again'; set the visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout; Lambda refuses a function timeout longer than the queue's visibility timeout. The case's consumer is a container worker, not Lambda, so this check does not protect it. That a standard queue delivers at least once (so consumers must be idempotent), the 30-second default visibility timeout and ChangeMessageVisibility are from memory of the SQS developer guide (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the solutions architect on call at Cobalt Lane, a fictional subscription box company. Orders go to the SQS standard queue order-events; ECS workers take each message, charge the card through the payment provider, write the order and delete the message. This morning's release added an invoice PDF to that work. Since then, support reports customers charged two or three times. The 14:00 subscription renewals put 40,000 messages on the queue.
handover: The workers call ReceiveMessage, do the work and then DeleteMessage; they do not extend visibility.
The payment provider accepts an idempotency key on each charge; the code does not send one today.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the queue, its visibility timeout and the workers that charge cards.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why customers were charged twice, what you changed, and why both changes are needed.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The PDF change made each message take 45-80 seconds, but order-events hides a received message for only 30. It reappeared and another worker charged it again; the charge carried no idempotency key.

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Fixes the timeout and the consumer, without losing orders.
parts.modelAnswer: VisibilityTimeout 300 seconds, above the slowest work, and the order ID as the provider's idempotency key. Purging would have deleted orders never charged.

parts.label: Both
parts.criteria: Knows a standard queue delivers at least once.
parts.modelAnswer: A standard queue can deliver a message twice even with a good timeout, so the consumer must be idempotent; the timeout stops the routine redelivery, the key makes any that remain harmless. Duplicates were refunded and an alarm watches redeliveries.

Visibility 300 s; idempotency key deployed; refunds and a redelivery alarm.

ordersLost.headline: Stopping duplicates by losing originals
ordersLost.body: The duplicates came from messages reappearing during work. Purging deletes the work itself. Lengthen the visibility timeout and make the charge idempotent.

renewalsDoubled.headline: At-least-once needs two defenses
renewalsDoubled.body: A visibility timeout shorter than the work causes redelivery; a charge without an idempotency key turns redelivery into a second charge. Fix both before load arrives.

idempotent.headline: Good: delivery and idempotency
idempotent.body: You measured the work against the visibility timeout, fixed the timeout and made the consumer idempotent (a standard queue can always deliver twice), checked it, and refunded the customers.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The release made each message take longer than the queue's 30-second visibility timeout, so messages reappeared during work and a second worker charged them again, with no idempotency key to stop it. Raise the visibility timeout above the slowest work and send the order ID as the charge's idempotency key, because a standard queue can deliver twice anyway. Purging loses real orders and long polling changes nothing. Then refund the duplicates and alarm on redeliveries.
